delta_summary.moral_floor: The week did not mark stability. It showed democratic erosion becoming more distributed, procedural, and normalized across multiple institutions at once.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: No net clock movement, but clear consolidation: power widened its use of existing channels while courts and civic actors provided only partial friction.

epigraphs.text: A republic weakens not only when rules are broken, but when they are reopened whenever power sees advantage.
Freedom narrows first at the edges: in records withheld, critics singled out, and procedures changed after the game begins.

long_synopsis: Week 68 brought no single rupture, but a broad reinforcement of anti-democratic patterns across many institutions at once. After a Supreme Court ruling weakened Voting Rights Act protections, Republican officials rapidly reopened redistricting fights, with Tennessee dismantling its only majority-Black congressional district and other states moving to redraw maps mid-cycle. Federal law enforcement and prosecutors increased pressure on critics, election workers, and political actors, while the Justice Department also sought to shield the president in a personal case. Regulators and investigators leaned on broadcasters, reporters, and news organizations through license reviews, leak probes, and lawsuits. Immigration enforcement intensified despite court limits, with re-arrests, deadly operations, harms to children, and long-term funding expansion. Abroad, war powers remained concentrated in the executive as military action, naming, costs, and evidence were managed through secrecy. The clock held steady because these were consolidations, not a fresh leap.
short_synopsis: The week deepened existing patterns rather than creating a new break: mid-cycle election changes, selective law enforcement, pressure on the press, harsher immigration enforcement, and executive secrecy around war. Courts still imposed some friction, but the dominant movement was consolidation.
